ready2_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Consider a step voltage of magnitude 1 pu travelling along a lossless transmission line that terminates in a reactor. The voltage magnitude across the reactor at the instant travelling wave reaches the reactor is ________ (pu)
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Consider a step voltage of magnitude 1 pu travelling along a lossless transmission line that terminates in a reactor. The voltage magnitude across the reactor at the instant travelling wave reaches the reactor is ________ (pu)
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the figure shows a step traveling wave propagating to the right along a lossless transmission line, arriving at endpoint A; endpoint A is grounded through a reactor labeled Reactor. Then reason: the problem statement gives the amplitude of the incident step voltage as 1 pu. At the instant when the traveling wave just reaches the reactor, the reactor current cannot change abruptly; if the initial current is zero, then this terminal is equivalent to an open circuit at this instant. The voltage reflection coefficient at an open-circuit terminal is Γv = +1, therefore the amplitude of the reflected voltage wave is also 1 pu. The endpoint voltage, namely the voltage across the reactor, is the sum of the incident voltage and the reflected voltage: 1 + 1 = 2 pu.

method.method_draft: Read the incident step magnitude as 1 pu from the text. From the image/text, identify the line termination as a grounded reactor. At the instant of first arrival, treat the reactor current as still zero, i.e. the termination is effectively open-circuited. Use Γv = +1 for an open circuit, so the reflected voltage wave is also 1 pu. Add incident and reflected voltages at the reactor terminal: 1 + 1 = 2 pu.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Direct transient-boundary route using the inductor's instantaneous open-circuit behavior and the voltage reflection coefficient.
planner_metadata.image_role: Use the diagram only to identify the termination: the travelling step reaches node A, which is connected through a reactor/inductor to ground.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the text for the given incident step voltage magnitude, 1 pu, and that the line is lossless and terminates in a reactor.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: For an inductor, current cannot change instantaneously; before the wave arrives the reactor current is zero, so at the first instant it behaves like an open circuit. An open-circuit line termination has voltage reflection coefficient +1, so terminal voltage equals incident plus reflected voltage.
